items.c: The symbol of the growing power of Japan's new leaders was the kofun burial mounds they constructed from around AD 250 onwards.
items.def: Kofun are megalithic tombs or tumuli in Northeast Asia.

items.c: Edo, also romanized as Jedo, Yedo or Yeddo, is the former name of Tokyo.
items.def: Edo, also romanized as Jedo, Yedo or Yeddo, is the former name of Tokyo.

items.c: The regime that Yoritomo had established, and which was kept in place by his successors, was decentralized and feudalistic in structure, in contrast with the earlier ritsuryō state.
items.def: Feudalism, also known as the feudal system, was a combination of various customs and systems that flourished in medieval Europe from the 9th to 15th centuries.

items.c: The Heian period is considered a golden age of classical Japanese culture. Japanese religious life from this time and onwards was a mix of native Shinto practices and Buddhism.
items.def: Japanese culture has changed greatly over the millennia, from the country's prehistoric Jōmon period, to its contemporary modern culture, which absorbs influences from Asia and other regions of the world.

items.c: After 1955, Japan enjoyed very high economic growth under the governance of the Liberal Democratic Party, and became a world economic powerhouse.
items.def: Japan has a highly developed mixed economy.

items.c: Hideyoshi's land survey designated all those who were cultivating the land as being "commoners", an act which effectively granted freedom to most of Japan's slaves.
items.def: Slavery in Japan existed in several forms from antiquity through the modern period, alongside and proceeding other systems of unfree and coerced labor, some manifestations of which continue to this day.

items.c: The Tokugawas sponsored and were heavily influenced by Neo-Confucianism, which led the government to divide society into four classes based on the four occupations.
items.def: The four occupations, or "four categories of the people", was an occupation classification used in ancient China by either Confucian or Legalist scholars as far back as the late Zhou dynasty and is considered a central part of the fengjian social structure.

items.c: Young people across the world began consuming kaiju (monster) movies, anime (animation), manga (comic books), video games, and other forms Japanese pop culture.
items.def: Anime is animation originating from Japan.

items.c: Despite Japan's economic difficulties, this period also saw Japanese popular culture, including video games, anime, and manga, expanding worldwide, especially among young people.
items.def: Manga are comics or graphic novels originating from Japan.

items.c: Maya royal succession was patrilineal, and royal power only passed to queens when doing otherwise would result in the extinction of the dynasty.
items.def: Patrilineality, also known as the male line, the spear side or agnatic kinship, is a common kinship system in which an individual's family membership derives from and is recorded through their father's lineage.

items.c: Indigenous cuisine of the Americas

items.c: Kingship was usually (but not exclusively) patrilineal, and power normally passed to the eldest son.

items.c: The upper façades of buildings were decorated with precut stones mosaic-fashion, erected as facing over the core, forming elaborate compositions of long-nosed deities such as the rain god Chaac and the Principal Bird Deity.

items.c: For the Maya, the heliacal rising of Venus was associated with destruction and upheaval.
